title: Security baselines: clean logs, redacted PII, TLS enforced, explicit CORS
asA: security reviewer signing off the service
iWant: secrets out of logs, PII redacted by stated policy, TLS mandatory outside development, and CORS deny-by-default
soThat: the defects functional tests never catch are closed by specification

acceptanceCriteria.description: No secret material (bearer tokens, API keys, passwords, session identifiers, idempotency keys) appears in log output at any level, including debug.
acceptanceCriteria.given: traffic exercising auth, sessions, and idempotency with logging at the most verbose level
acceptanceCriteria.when: all log output is scanned for the known secret values

acceptanceCriteria.description: The PII-redaction policy is stated in project documentation, naming the field classes it covers and the redaction form, and log and error output conform to it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the stated policy and traffic carrying PII fields
acceptanceCriteria.when: logs and error responses are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: every covered field class appears only in its declared redacted form

acceptanceCriteria.description: In non-development environments the service is reachable only over TLS: plain HTTP is refused or redirected, and no listener serves business endpoints in cleartext.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a plain HTTP request is attempted
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused or redirected to TLS and no cleartext business response is served

acceptanceCriteria.description: CORS is deny-by-default: a cross-origin request from an undeclared origin receives no permissive CORS headers, and no wildcard origin is served on any credentialed endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a cross-origin request from an origin not on the declared allowlist
acceptanceCriteria.then: no Access-Control-Allow-Origin permits the undeclared origin, and no credentialed endpoint ever serves a wildcard

acceptanceCriteria.description: Per-endpoint CORS overrides are declared configuration: an endpoint allowing specific origins lists them, the declaration is auditable alongside the endpoint, and behaviour matches it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an endpoint with a declared CORS override
acceptanceCriteria.when: cross-origin requests from declared and undeclared origins arrive
acceptanceCriteria.then: declared origins succeed per the declaration and undeclared origins are refused

acceptanceCriteria.description: Problem-details responses never leak internals: stack traces, SQL, file paths, and dependency hostnames are absent from every error body in non-development environments.
acceptanceCriteria.given: induced 4xx and 5xx errors in a non-development configuration
acceptanceCriteria.then: no stack trace, query text, filesystem path, or internal hostname appears
